Varint encoding works by:
- Using 7 bits per byte for the actual value
- Using the 8th bit as a continuation flag (1 means more bytes follow, 0 means this is the last byte)
- The maximum length for a uint64_t is 10 bytes (since 64/7 = 9.14, so we need 10 bytes to represent the largest 64-bit value)

The implementation should count how many 7-bit chunks are needed. I can do this by repeatedly shifting the value right by 7 bits until it becomes 0, counting the number of shifts needed.
